# 1494 Labs

# Fund, partnership and portfolio accounting for fund managers, allocators and fund administrators.

## [Who it is for](https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-software/)

- Managers (GPs): hedge funds, private equity, credit and real estate funds, registered funds, RICs and BDCs. Fund and investor accounting, fees, waterfalls and carry, investor statements and regulatory filings.

- Allocators (LPs): fund of funds, family offices, endowments, foundations and other institutional investors. Commitments, calls and distributions across every underlying fund, look-through to the holdings, and performance by vintage, strategy and manager.

- Administrators: many funds with different terms on one platform, and reconciliation against bank, custodian and administrator files.

- [Fund, Partnership and Investor Accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-software/)

- [Hedge Fund Accounting](https://1494labs.com/hedge-fund-accounting/)

- [Private Equity Fund Accounting](https://1494labs.com/private-equity-fund-accounting/)

- [Registered Fund Accounting](https://1494labs.com/registered-fund-accounting/)

- [Family Office Accounting](https://1494labs.com/family-office-accounting/)

- [Fund Administration Software](https://1494labs.com/fund-administration-software/)

- [Fund of Funds Accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/)

- [Investment Accounting for Endowments and Foundations](https://1494labs.com/endowment-foundation-accounting/)

## [Partnership and investor accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-software/)

- Subscriptions, redemptions, transfers, calls, commitments, distributions and recallable capital.

- Equalization or series accounting, chosen per fund. High-water marks carried per investor through partial redemptions, transfers and restatements.

- Management and incentive fees, offsets, waterfalls with carry, clawback and vesting, and side pockets.

- Allocations by class, series and sleeve, and investor NAV in the class currency.

## [Complex structures](https://1494labs.com/holding-company-and-family-office-entity-accounting/)

- Master-feeder, alternative investment vehicles (AIVs), SPVs, blockers, co-investments and continuation vehicles.

- Holding companies, family partnerships, trusts and GRATs, SMAs and funds of one, and personal accounts, with ownership traced through every layer.

- Blocker tax accrued at the entity and carried to each investor behind it.

- Fund of funds look-through to the underlying holdings, on both ownership bases.

## [Portfolio accounting across asset classes](https://1494labs.com/portfolio-accounting/)

- Public and private equity, fixed income, loans, credit facilities on both sides, real estate and REITs, derivatives, hedge fund and private fund interests, and digital assets, in any currency.

## [Portfolio companies](https://1494labs.com/portfolio-company-kpi-collection/)

- Financials and KPIs collected from each company by upload or a secure submission link: revenue, EBITDA, net debt and the metrics you define, checked on the way in.

- Every submission and correction kept with its reporting date, currency, source and submitter.

- Collected figures shown beside each valuation mark, and the submission used recorded with it.

- Cap tables with financing rounds, tenders, vesting and exit waterfalls.

- Company financials and KPIs in fund reporting, with missing companies flagged.

## [Secondaries](https://1494labs.com/secondaries-and-strip-sale-accounting/)

- Buy and sell LP interests, single or as a strip sale across many funds in one transaction.

- Purchase-price adjustments and deferred payments at a discount, with interim flows between the reference date and closing.

- The day-one gain between price paid and fair value recognized at acquisition, and cost basis kept.

- GP-led deals: continuation vehicles and tender offers.

- Direct secondaries in common stock, valued with waterfall and option-pricing methods.

- A secondaries portfolio report, and buyer and seller confirmations.

## [Liquidity and forecasting](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/)

- Cash projection in horizon buckets out past a year, from settled cash: expected proceeds from underlying funds, investor outflows, unfunded commitments and scheduled obligations.

- Available liquidity including undrawn credit facilities.

- Commitment pacing for fund of funds and allocator programs.

- Deployment and exit forecasts for drawdown funds, with fees and fund-level debt.

- Cash-flow plans for evergreen, real estate and credit books: dealing, property recoveries, loan draws, interest and repayments.

- Scenarios with frozen inputs, each projected amount traced to the records behind it, and past forecasts kept.

- Gates, lockups and notice periods tracked for every underlying fund.

## [Close, controls and reconciliation](https://1494labs.com/close-controls-and-reconciliation/)

- Period close with a frozen trial balance and graded revisions.

- Official and latest-knowledge books on one ledger, with the source of every line.

- Cash, positions and NAV reconciled against outside files, with an exceptions worklist.

- A check that recomputes every fund's arithmetic each morning.

## [Reporting](https://1494labs.com/fund-and-investor-reporting/)

- NAV, capital account statements, ILPA notices, performance, and Form PF and Form ADV answers from the same book.

- Saved analyses that refresh on the platform and can be pulled through the API.

## [API and AI](https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-api-and-ai/)

- Everything on screen is also in the public API.

- AI assistants read the book through MCP.

- AI reads statements and LPAs, and a person confirms each result before it posts.

The capability matrix lists product scope and status.

## Demo, sandbox and assistant access

- [Request a demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact): describe your fund and current workflow, or email hello@1494labs.com. Ask for a sandbox seeded with reference funds.
- [Capabilities](https://1494labs.com/capabilities.md): current product scope and status.
- [Connect an assistant](https://1494labs.com/connect-assistant.md): endpoint, authentication, tools and a synthetic example.
- MCP: POST /api/v1/mcp on your workspace's application origin. Requires ordinary workspace authentication and respects the user's permissions. Tools read the book and run saved analyses; this is not an anonymous public demo endpoint. Ask hello@1494labs.com about connecting your assistant.

## Pages and worked notes

Source: https://1494labs.com/blocker-corporation-accounting/

# Blocker Corporation Accounting

For fund managers, allocators and administrators accounting for investors through blockers.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Blocker setup records the corporation, its underlying fund or AIV investment and the investors behind it. Federal and state tax rates are configured per blocker. Period tax accrual posts an entity-level expense and tax payable; configured deferred tax covers unrealized gains.

- Fund setup provides a Blocker vehicle type, federal and state tax-rate fields, and a choice to accrue deferred tax on unrealized gains. The blocker's fund page shows its period accrual and tax payable.

- The underlying fund allocates the blocker's share before corporate tax. Investors behind the blocker receive their ownership share after the entity's tax expense. A direct LP and a blocker LP can therefore have the same gross allocation and different net amounts.

- Investor statements show both gross allocation and blocker tax. The current-tax expense and payable are posted in the blocker's ledger, and configured deferred tax is carried as a separate accrual.

- Ownership and exposure reports follow the corporation's investment through the underlying fund or alternative investment vehicle to the holdings. The investors behind the blocker remain part of that ownership chain.

## Terms

Blocker and corporate feeder describe the corporation through which US tax-exempt and non-US investors invest. UBTI means unrelated business taxable income; ECI means effectively connected income. Entity-level tax and deferred tax are recorded on the corporation's books.

## Questions

### Does the product account for blocker corporations?

Yes. A blocker is a separate vehicle with its own configured federal and state rates. Period tax accrual posts expense and tax payable on the blocker's books. Deferred tax on unrealized gains is accrued when configured.

### Can investors behind a blocker see gross allocation and tax?

Yes. The blocker's capital account in the underlying fund carries the pre-tax allocation. Each investor behind the corporation carries a share net of blocker tax. Investor statements show the gross allocation and the blocker tax.

### Can I configure federal, state and deferred tax per blocker?

Yes. Federal and state rates are set for each blocker, and deferred tax is enabled per blocker. The accrual records current tax on allocated taxable income and remeasures configured deferred tax on unrealized gains.

### Can ownership reports look through the blocker to holdings?

Yes. The blocker participates in the ownership chain. Look-through and exposure reports trace the investors' ownership through the corporation and the underlying fund or AIV to the recorded holdings.

### Does this include corporate tax return preparation?

No. The blocker accounting scope covers configured-rate accruals, tax payables, deferred tax and the investor allocation. Corporate tax returns, including Form 1120 and K-1 preparation, and additional withholding regimes are outside this scope.

### Can I see the tax accrual and payable in the product?

Yes. The blocker's fund page provides the period tax accrual and payable view. The accrual action posts the tax expense and payable on the blocker's books, with current and configured deferred amounts recorded for the selected period.

# Capital Call and Distribution Software

For fund managers, allocators and administrators tracking investor commitments and cash flows.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Investor bank details have a change-and-approval workflow. Account details are masked in the investor screen; revealing them requires permission. Approved details supply the bank information used in notices.

- Capital call notices are available as PDFs through the API. The notice carries the investor's amount, due date and wire instructions from approved bank details, for the accounting team's call-notice process.

- Distribution notices are available as PDFs through the API. Each notice belongs to a recorded distribution and provides the investor-facing document for that cash event.

- Capital Accounts shows unfunded commitments by investor and fund. A fund setting chooses the historical or spot measure, so the reported unfunded amount follows the accounting basis selected for that fund.

- Capital Accounts shows investor balances for the selected fund. Accounting checks compare investor capital snapshots with general ledger capital, giving the investor balances a defined tie to the fund's capital accounts.

- Investor statements show opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expenses, fees and ending capital. The statement draws these amounts from the investor's recorded account and the fund's reporting period.

## Terms

Commitment budget, called capital and unfunded commitment describe an investor's funding position. Recallable capital and distributions recycled describe returned amounts that the fund terms permit to be called again.

## Questions

### Can I retrieve a capital call notice through the API?

Yes. The capital call notice endpoint returns a PDF with the investor's amount, due date and wire instructions. Wire instructions come from approved bank details. The notice is retrieved through the API.

### Can I retrieve an investor distribution notice?

Yes. The distribution notice endpoint returns the PDF for a recorded distribution. It provides the investor-facing notice for that distribution through the API.

### Can I see unfunded commitments by investor?

Yes. Capital Accounts reports unfunded commitments per investor and per fund. The fund's setting selects the historical or spot measure used in that view, giving the team a defined basis for the outstanding amount.

### Are changes to investor bank details approved?

Yes. Bank-detail changes require a second person's approval. The investor screen masks the stored details, and revealing them requires a separate permission. Notices use the approved bank details.

### Do investor capital accounts tie to general ledger capital?

Yes. The accounting checks compare investor capital balances with the fund's general ledger capital. Capital Accounts displays the investor balances. The tie is an accounting invariant checked across the book.

# Close, Controls and Reconciliation

For controllers and administrators closing funds and reviewing reconciliation exceptions.

## Period Close and Ledger Controls

- Journal Entries shows the postings created by accounting transactions. Each journal entry retains its source type and source identifier. The entry detail displays the accounting lines and the recorded transaction source.

- Period Close records period opening, closing and locking events. Reopening requires permission and a recorded reason. The period's event history keeps the actions recorded for a revised close.

- Period Close includes a checklist and reviewer sign-off. A period lock requires the configured sign-off, so the recorded review forms part of the close process before the books are locked.

- NAV records preliminary, final and restated fund values, including share-class lines. The NAV and period-close screens show the fund's strike workflow, with class results available through the share register.

- Capital Accounts shows investor balances for the selected fund. Accounting checks compare investor capital snapshots with general ledger capital, giving the investor balances a defined tie to the fund's capital accounts.

- Allocations distributes income, expenses and gains through recorded ownership. The allocation screen includes a cascade preview and confirmation for structures with multiple ownership layers, connecting fund results with the investors above them.

- Reporting provides the trial balance for the fund, including the balance frozen at close and its revisions. The frozen balance preserves the ledger totals used for that close and subsequent review.

## Related Notes

- [Checking the book against outside records](https://1494labs.com/notes/a-wrong-number-that-agrees-with-itself/)

- [ABOR and IBOR](https://1494labs.com/notes/abor-and-ibor/)

- [Converting from a fund administrator](https://1494labs.com/notes/converting-from-a-fund-administrator/)

## Questions

### Can I identify the transaction behind a journal entry?

Yes. Each journal entry records a source type and source identifier. Journal Entries displays the posting detail and source label; underlying distribution entries also have a direct link to the source transaction.

### Can a closed period be reopened with a recorded reason?

Yes. Period Close supports a governed reopen action for users with reopen permission. The reason is recorded with the event, and the period history retains the closing, locking and reopening actions.

### Can reviewer sign-off gate the period lock?

Yes. The close checklist and review events are recorded for the period. Locking checks that the required sign-off is present, and the reviewer's action remains in the period history.

### Do investor capital accounts tie to general ledger capital?

Yes. The accounting checks compare investor capital balances with the fund's general ledger capital. Capital Accounts displays the investor balances. The tie is an accounting invariant checked across the book.

### Can I retrieve the trial balance frozen at close?

Yes. Reporting includes frozen trial balances and revisions. The frozen balance keeps the ledger totals frozen at the close, so a reviewer can inspect the recorded close and the revisions attached to it.

# 1494 Labs vs Allvue Fund Accounting

A fund accounting comparison for a private equity team closing the ledger and investor capital accounts together. Use a worked close to test the fit.

Product sources reviewed November 3, 2026

## Start with the accounting workflow

Allvue describes cloud fund accounting for private equity and fund administrators, with a multi-currency general ledger, partnership accounting and financial reporting. Source: [Allvue Fund Accounting product page](https://www.allvuesystems.com/solutions/fund-accounting/), reviewed November 3, 2026.

1494 Labs configures fees, allocations and waterfalls to the fund's agreement. Investment records and investor capital accounts meet in one ledger, with recurring checks and a trail from a reported balance to its entries. See the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) for current product scope.

## What to compare in a demonstration

| Workflow | Allvue Fund Accounting: published description | 1494 Labs: demonstration to request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The accounting record | It describes a multi-currency general ledger and partnership accounting. [Source](https://www.allvuesystems.com/solutions/fund-accounting/) | 1494 Labs keeps investment and investor accounting on one ledger. Trace a capital account to its allocations and entries. |
| Fees and allocations | Its optional waterfall module models LPA terms and carry calculations. [Source](https://www.allvuesystems.com/solutions/fund-accounting/) | Configure fees and waterfalls to the fund's agreement, then inspect the calculation and the entries it produces. |
| Reviewing the result | It describes a financial report library, a flexible report writer and standardized workflows. [Source](https://www.allvuesystems.com/solutions/fund-accounting/) | Trace reported balances to the book and review the recurring checks that raise exceptions when the records stop tying. |

## Prove a private equity close from source to statement

Choose one fund with contributions, expenses and an investment exit. Configure its agreement terms, calculate the allocation and distribution, and trace the investor statement to the ledger. Include a correction in the open period and confirm that the calculation and its entries can be reviewed again.

1. Agree the opening book, governing terms and expected results before the demonstration.

2. Run the same dated transactions and valuations in each evaluation.

3. Compare fees, investor allocations and closing balances, with an explanation for every difference.

4. Ask to follow a reported amount back through its calculation and ledger entries.

Take the expected results away with the calculation evidence. The review should show whether the proposed setup handles your fund's terms and whether your team can explain the close.

[Request a 1494 Labs demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact) with your fund structure and one close you want to reproduce. You can also read [1494 Labs as an alternative to Allvue](https://1494labs.com/compare/allvue-alternative/) or [browse the comparison guides](https://1494labs.com/compare/).

## Compare waterfall results under the fund's agreement

Bring two exits with different dates and a later capital call. Specify whether the waterfall is whole-of-fund or deal-by-deal, and agree the preferred-return and catch-up terms. 3. Compare fees, investor allocations and closing balances, with an explanation for every difference.

4. Ask to follow a reported amount back through its calculation and ledger entries.

# 1494 Labs vs FundCount

A fund accounting comparison for a family office or fund team keeping investment and investor records together. Use a worked close to test the fit.

Product sources reviewed November 3, 2026

## Start with the accounting workflow

FundCount describes partnership and portfolio accounting posted to the same general ledger, including capital accounts, allocations and waterfalls. Source: [FundCount partnership accounting](https://fundcount.com/solutions/partnership-accounting/), reviewed November 3, 2026.

1494 Labs configures fees, allocations and waterfalls to the fund's agreement. Investment records and investor capital accounts meet in one ledger, with recurring checks and a trail from a reported balance to its entries. See the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) for current product scope.

## What to compare in a demonstration

| Workflow | FundCount: published description | 1494 Labs: demonstration to request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The accounting record | Capital activity and partner allocations post to its general ledger. [Source](https://fundcount.com/solutions/partnership-accounting/) | 1494 Labs keeps investment and investor accounting on one ledger. Trace a capital account to its allocations and entries. |
| Fees and allocations | Its partnership page describes configurable preferred returns, catch-up and carry splits. [Source](https://fundcount.com/solutions/partnership-accounting/) | Configure fees and waterfalls to the fund's agreement, then inspect the calculation and the entries it produces. |
| Reviewing the result | It describes on-demand capital statements and partner-level rollforwards. [Source](https://fundcount.com/solutions/partnership-accounting/) | Trace reported balances to the book and review the recurring checks that raise exceptions when the records stop tying. |

## Work through a multi-entity capital movement

Use a parent entity, an investment vehicle and two participating investors. Post an investment valuation, an expense and a distribution. Follow each investor's share through the ownership structure, then reconcile the entity balances and consolidated view. Change one source amount and review the resulting allocations and entries.

1. Agree the opening book, governing terms and expected results before the demonstration.

2. Run the same dated transactions and valuations in each evaluation.

3. Compare fees, investor allocations and closing balances, with an explanation for every difference.

4. Ask to follow a reported amount back through its calculation and ledger entries.

Take the expected results away with the calculation evidence. The review should show whether the proposed setup handles your fund's terms and whether your team can explain the close.

# Connect an assistant to your fund accounting workspace

Ask about funds and saved analyses through MCP, the standard connector for AI tools. Reads use your workspace permissions.

Connection guide · November 3, 2026

## What you need

An existing 1494 Labs workspace, an administrator who has enabled AI for that workspace, and an MCP client that supports Streamable HTTP with a custom Authorization header. This connection reads workspace data. There is no anonymous demo endpoint.

1. **Enable workspace AI.** An administrator enables AI under Administration › Workspace › AI & budget. When AI is off, MCP returns HTTP 403 with `ai_disabled`.

2. **Create a read-only key.** Under Administration › People & access › API Keys, choose Read-only or the specific read permissions you need. The key remains bound to its workspace and its creator's permissions. Copy the secret when shown and keep it in your client's credential store.

3. **Set the connection URL.** Use your workspace's application origin followed by `/api/v1/mcp`. For example, if you sign in at `https://your-workspace.example.com`, the URL is `https://your-workspace.example.com/api/v1/mcp`. Replace this illustrative origin with your actual workspace address; the marketing site is not the endpoint.

4. **Configure authentication.** Set `Authorization: Bearer <your-workspace-api-key>`. Use the Bearer header for this connection so credentials reach downstream reads. The endpoint also accepts a live session access token. Browser sessions use their access cookie and require the matching `X-CSRF-Token` on POST requests.

5. **Connect and discover tools.** Your client initializes the connection and lists tools. Start with `list_funds`, then discover the reads or saved analyses needed for your question.

Use a client that lets you supply the header. This endpoint does not provide an OAuth sign-in flow. If your assistant only offers OAuth connections, ask [hello@1494labs.com](mailto:hello@1494labs.com) about a compatible setup. Share credentials only through the client's credential settings, never in a conversation.

## The five tools

| Tool | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `list_funds` | Find funds by code or name and resolve their UUIDs. Optional `q` filters the list; `limit` controls the page size. |
| `search_api` | Find GET endpoints by a phrase such as "trial balance" or "capital account." Returns paths and parameters for a subsequent read. |
| `read_api` | Read a discovered `/api/v1/` path, passing its filters in `query`. Substitute real IDs for path placeholders and follow the endpoint's pagination when needed. |
| `list_saved_calcs` | Find saved analyses. Call without arguments for available grid keys, then pass a `grid_key` to list analyses on that table. Another user's private analyses are excluded. |
| `run_saved_calc` | Recompute an accessible saved analysis from the live book using its `calc_id`. Optional `fund_id`, `period_id` and `as_of` override its saved context. An empty subtotal with a reason is not zero. |

## A first question and answer

**Question:** "Which fund matches DEMO-PE? Tell me its legal name and currency."

The assistant calls `list_funds` with `{"q":"DEMO-PE","limit":10}`. Suppose the returned fund has `fund_code` DEMO-PE, `legal_name` Example Private Equity Fund LP and `base_currency_code` USD.

**Illustrative answer:** "DEMO-PE is Example Private Equity Fund LP. Its base currency is USD. Source: the workspace fund record returned by list_funds." These synthetic names and values illustrate the response. If several funds match, the assistant should ask which one you mean.

For an accounting question, keep that fund's returned `id`, use `search_api` to find the relevant read, then call `read_api` with the fund ID and the endpoint's required period parameters. Ask the assistant to name the fund, period and source, and to say when data is missing.

## Check the connection directly

A compatible client sends JSON-RPC 2.0 messages by HTTP POST with `Content-Type: application/json` and `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`. For example, after setting the URL and Bearer header in its connection settings, it sends:

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"workspace-reader","version":"1.0"}}}
```

Read the negotiated protocol version in the response, send `notifications/initialized` without an ID, then `tools/list`:

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}
```

The initialized notification returns HTTP 202 with no body. Calls return JSON. The server keeps no MCP session and has no server-push stream; a GET to the connection URL returns HTTP 405. Opening the URL in a browser is not a connection test.

## Access and troubleshooting

- **HTTP 401:** check the key or session token, its expiry and revocation state, and the workspace origin.

- **HTTP 403:** check the workspace AI setting and the permissions needed by the requested read. Seeing a tool name does not grant access to its data.

- **A tool reports an error:** check the returned reason, fund and period IDs, and the endpoint parameters. Do not turn a failed or truncated read into a financial answer.

These tools read data and compute saved results. They cannot create journals, post allocations or change fund terms. Revoking or rotating the key ends its use under the workspace's normal key policy. Choose an assistant approved by your organization for the data you intend to read.

[Request a demo or sandbox](https://1494labs.com/#contact) to try this on reference funds. See the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) for current product scope.


---

Source: https://1494labs.com/distribution-waterfall-software/

# Distribution waterfalls configured from the agreement

The waterfall decides how every distribution splits between limited partners and the GP. It is also where fund accounting most often moves into a spreadsheet, because the system's version of the waterfall is a dropdown and the agreement's version is four pages of defined terms.

Private equity · roughly 6 minutes

## Seven answers define a waterfall

Most waterfall settings offer "European" and "American" and stop there. The agreements we read are usually somewhere in between. These seven questions reconstruct almost any of them:

1. Are the tiers measured against the fund or against each investment?

2. Does the preferred return compound, and on what base? Does it accrue on fees as well as capital?

3. Is there a loss carryforward, and does it cover unrealized write-downs or only realized losses?

4. What is the catch-up rate, and is it 100%?

5. Is there an escrow, at what percentage, and when does it release?

6. Is clawback gross or after-tax, and is it guaranteed by individuals?

7. How often is the interim clawback test run?

A waterfall here is an ordered set of tiers, each with its own parameters, and the answers go straight into them. The two named conventions are starting configurations you then edit. Every field is chosen from a fixed list of options with a stated meaning, so there is no formula to get wrong.

## Test the terms before they govern money

The builder has a sample calculation beside it. Type in hypothetical distributions and it runs them through the same calculation the fund will use, as you edit. It's the quickest way to find out what an 80% catch-up does to the GP's share before it applies to anybody's money.

![The waterfall builder: a named set of conventions, a stack of tiers with carry and catch-up rates, and a sample calculation panel computing preferred accrued of $46,932,807.68 and a catch-up band from hypothetical distributions.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/waterfall-worked-example.957ef3d5.jpg)

**The terms, tested before they are terms.** The panel computes accrued preferred and the catch-up band from hypothetical cash, using the policy as it currently stands.

## One distribution, through four tiers

The reference fund's policy has four tiers: return of capital, accrued preferred at 8% net of returned capital, a GP catch-up to 20% at a 100% rate, then an 80/20 split, measured whole-of-fund.

A distribution of $12,075,209.34 runs through it. $9,300,000.00 goes back to the limited partners as capital, and $153,070.79 goes to the GP as carry. Each limited partner's share posts to their capital account, and the distribution carries ILPA component codes from the moment it is posted.

![A waterfall policy with four tiers, a clawback measurement per LP showing no exposure, and a posted distribution of $12,075,209.34: $9,300,000.00 returned as capital and $153,070.79 of GP carry.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/distribution-waterfall.446c8f15.jpg)

**The posted distribution, with clawback exposure beside the policy.** Exposure is measured per LP by default.

## Carry stays provisional until the fund proves it

Carry paid early can turn out to be overpaid. On the same two deals, an American waterfall can pay a GP $10m of carry in year 3 that the fund, measured whole, only ever earned $4m of. [That example is worked through in full here](https://1494labs.com/notes/european-vs-american-waterfall/).

So carry is held as an accrual subject to the whole-fund test, and clawback exposure is a figure the ledger already carries. An interim clawback test reads straight off the screen at any period end, which means an overpayment shows up in the year it happens.

## Who the carry belongs to

Once carry reaches the GP, it is split among the principals, and each principal's share vests per principal. LP givebacks are recorded alongside clawback. [GP economics in the product docs](https://docs.1494labs.com/guide/gp-economics/) covers how the split and the vesting work.

## What it doesn't do

The platform runs the waterfall at the fund level and doesn't call any configuration "compliant" with your agreement. Your LPA is the authority, and the configuration is your reading of it. Tax allocations of carry, and the K-1s that report them, stay with your tax preparer.

## Related reading

- [American vs European waterfall on the same two deals](https://1494labs.com/notes/european-vs-american-waterfall/)

- [Private equity fund accounting](https://1494labs.com/private-equity-fund-accounting/)

- [Capital calls and distributions](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/)

- [What an opening balance has to carry](https://1494labs.com/notes/what-an-opening-balance-has-to-carry/), for a fund moving systems partway through its waterfall

- [GP economics](https://docs.1494labs.com/guide/gp-economics/) in the product docs

## Show us the waterfall that breaks your current system

Send us the distribution section of the agreement. We will configure it in front of you and run your last distribution through it, or stand up a sandbox with reference funds for you to try it yourself.

[Request a demo](https://1494labs.com/?segment=pevc#contact)

Source: https://1494labs.com/endowment-foundation-accounting/

# Investment accounting for endowments and foundations

An endowment's investment office usually runs a multi-asset pool with a large private fund program inside it. The public side is reported by a custodian. The private side arrives one manager statement at a time, each at its own date, and has to be carried, reconciled and paced against the cash the pool will need.

Endowments and foundations · roughly 4 minutes

## One book for the whole pool

Public securities, private fund interests and direct holdings sit on one multi-asset book. Positions reconcile against the custodian's file, and cash reconciles against imported bank statements. A statement line matches the book automatically only when exactly one movement fits it. Anything else is left for a person, and whatever is left over opens an exception on the same worklist as everything else.

![Two open reconciliation exceptions for one endowment fund's operating cash at 30 June 2026: an unmatched bank line of $2,150.00 and the balance difference it causes, each 32 days old.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/reconciliation-breaks.3b91eb16.jpg)

**What is left over becomes an exception.** An unmatched bank line and the balance difference it causes, open on the worklist with their age.

## The private program, with its dates showing

Each fund interest carries the as-of date and source of its last NAV statement. Late statements and estimate-to-final true-ups are booked as corrections, so a closed quarter can be corrected without disturbing what was already reported to the investment committee. Each position shows IRR, TVPI, DPI and RVPI.

![Portfolio holdings of private fund interests: six named underlying managers, each with cost, value, the date it was last valued and a link to its marks.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/portfolio-holdings.3916f10a.jpg)

**Six managers, each at cost and at value.** The date each was last revalued sits on the row, because the age of an input is part of the number.

## What the pool actually holds

Look-through shows the companies underneath your fund interests, grouped by sector and geography, from holdings the managers report, as of any date you choose. [Fund of funds accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/) covers how look-through works and what happens when a manager doesn't report the size it needs.

## Pacing the commitments

Unfunded commitments are shown by fund, and the liquidity projection sets expected calls against cash and available undrawn credit. [Commitment pacing and liquidity forecasting](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/) covers the forecast.

## What we don't do

We keep the investment pool's books: the pool, every endowed fund's share of it, including its net asset class (with or without donor restrictions) and its spending-policy payouts. Your institution's general ledger stays in its ERP, fed by mapped entries. We don't hold custody or move money, and market data comes from your own provider.

## Related reading

- [Fund of funds accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/)

- [Liquidity forecasting and commitment pacing](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/)

- [Checking the book against outside records](https://1494labs.com/notes/a-wrong-number-that-agrees-with-itself/)

- [Capabilities and status](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/)

Tell us how the pool is structured and how manager statements reach the office. We will walk you through a quarter in the product, or stand up a sandbox for you to work in.

# Equalization and Series Accounting

For hedge fund managers and administrators with investors entering at different dates.

## Equalization, Series and High-Water Marks

- Equalization factor or series accounting is chosen per fund. Equalization records the adjustment linked to an investor's subscription. Series accounting keeps subscription cohorts and their performance-fee history, with series consolidation and a preview of the consolidation amounts.

- High-water marks are carried per investor and per series. A partial redemption preserves the continuing investor's fee history; transfers carry the relevant mark and loss history. The incentive-fee calculation uses the configured hurdle and high-water mark.

## Supporting Accounting

- Share classes hold the terms for unitized funds. Fee classes group investors in capital-based funds. The Share Classes and Fee Terms screens record these arrangements for funds whose investors have different fee terms.

- The Fees screen calculates period management fees from the fund's saved terms. Accruals can be posted and reversed, giving the period fee a corresponding accounting entry in the fund's books.

- Investor statements show opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expenses, fees and ending capital. The statement draws these amounts from the investor's recorded account and the fund's reporting period.

- NAV supports share-class and series values, with final period strikes and daily estimates. Daily NAV estimates retain their grade and are superseded by the period close, preserving the distinction between daily and closed values.

## Terms

Equalization and series accounting are performance-fee terms for investors entering at different dates. Buyers also use high-water mark, hurdle, crystallization, equalization credit and series roll-up.

## Related Notes

- [Equalization and the mid-period subscriber](https://1494labs.com/notes/equalization-and-the-mid-period-subscriber/)

- [High-water marks and partial redemptions](https://1494labs.com/notes/high-water-marks-and-partial-redemptions/)

## Questions

### Can I choose equalization or series accounting per fund?

Yes. Fund terms select the performance-fee approach. Equalization records subscription-linked adjustments, including credits or deposits under the selected terms. Series accounting keeps cohorts with their own fee history and supports consolidation with a preview.

### Does a partial redemption preserve the investor's high-water mark?

Yes. The continuing holding retains its high-water-mark history after a partial redemption. Transfer records carry the relevant marks and loss history. Incentive-fee and crystallization records use the investor's configured hurdle and fee terms.

### Can I keep daily NAV estimates and final class NAV?

Yes. NAV supports daily estimates and final period strikes with share-class and series values. Daily estimates carry an estimate grade and are superseded by the close when final NAV is struck.

### Can investors in one fund have different fee terms?

Yes. Unitized funds use share classes, and capital-based funds use fee classes. The Share Classes and Fee Terms screens record these groups and their terms within the fund.

### Can I inspect the adjustment for a mid-period subscriber?

Yes. Equalization records link the adjustment to the subscription and retain the entry values used in its calculation. Adjustment detail shows the recorded credit or deposit. Series funds retain the subscription cohort and its performance-fee history.

## Related Accounting Pages

- [Fund of Funds Accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/)

- [Capital Call and Distribution Software](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/)

- [Liquidity Forecasting and Commitment Pacing](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/)

- [Fund Accounting Glossary](https://1494labs.com/glossary/)

# Family office accounting, through every layer of ownership

A family's wealth usually sits several entities deep. A trust owns part of a holding company, the holding company owns a family partnership, and the partnership holds the funds, the companies and the co-investments. The accounting question is what the family actually owns once those layers are taken out.

Family office · roughly 5 minutes

## Count each asset once

In the reference household below, the legal books of every vehicle add up to $12.01bn. The family owns $1.50bn of it. The difference is the same money counted again at each layer it passes through.

Each row in the consolidation carries the effective ownership that got it there, and that ownership is computed from the capital accounts. Forty percent of a $157.5m holding company is $63.0m, and the ledger knows it is forty percent because that is what the capital accounts say. The consolidation and the ownership chart are built from the same numbers, so they can't drift apart.

[How look-through consolidation works, with the full example](https://1494labs.com/family-office-consolidation/)

![A look-through consolidation showing legal books of $12.01bn against a consolidated $1.50bn, with a per-asset table giving legal owner, asset class, valuation basis, effective ownership, gross value and attributed value.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/look-through-consolidation.a6726248.jpg)

**$12.01bn of legal books, $1.50bn of it actually owned.** Every row shows its legal owner, its valuation basis and the effective ownership behind its attributed value.

## The structure lives in the ledger

Holding companies, family partnerships, trusts, GRATs, personal accounts and individuals are all vehicle types. Ownership weights come from capital holdings, so when a trust distributes or a sibling's interest changes, the structure chart and the allocations move with the capital.

Income, expenses and gains cascade up through the ownership chain, including where one vehicle has several owners. The allocation screen previews the cascade before you confirm it.

![The whole ownership structure as an org chart: four trusts, a holding company, a family partnership, six asset vehicles and a co-investment vehicle.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/structure-graph.60cc35a2.jpg)

**Every vehicle once, with its owners converging on it.** A vehicle with several owners appears once, where a set of separate trees would repeat it on every branch.

## Trusts and their beneficiaries

Beneficiary interests are recorded against the trust that holds them. The net worth view shows each beneficiary's interest beside the trust, so a principal can see what sits in trust for each family member without a separate schedule.

## Private funds and companies inside the family

Family vehicles hold LP interests in outside funds, direct company stakes and co-investments. Capital calls and distributions on those fund interests are booked against the vehicle that holds them. Fund NAV statements are recorded with an as-of date and a source, and company marks carry a valuation method, so the age of every input is on the page.

A family with a large private fund program usually needs two more things: a view through each fund to the companies underneath it, and a forecast of the cash its commitments will draw. [Fund of funds accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/) covers the first and [commitment pacing](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/) covers the second.

## What the family sees

Net worth by asset category, by holder and by period, with the movement between periods. Household performance, principal cash flows, exposure and concentration, and a reconciliation of book value to market value.

Report packs are organized by audience, so a pack for the principals and a pack for the trustees can run off the same book for the same period. Each exports to PDF or CSV.

## What we don't do

We keep the books. We don't hold custody or move money: the platform produces the payment file, and someone on your team takes it to the bank. Tax returns and K-1s stay with your preparer. Market data comes from your own provider, loaded through a connection we maintain.

- [Fund of funds accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/)

- [Liquidity forecasting and commitment pacing](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/)

- [Capital calls and distributions](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/)

- [Capabilities and status](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/)

Tell us how the family is organized, and we will walk you through it in the product on a running book. If you want to try it yourself, we will stand up a sandbox seeded with a reference household.

# Look-through consolidation for family offices

Add up the balance sheets of every entity a family owns and the total is wrong, sometimes by a factor of eight. Every layer of ownership counts the layer beneath it again. Consolidated reporting is the work of taking those duplicates out so each asset is counted once, at the share the family actually holds.

Family office · roughly 6 minutes

## Why the legal books overstate

Take a small chain. A trust owns 40% of a holding company. The holding company owns 60% of a family partnership. The partnership holds a $100m interest in an outside fund.

That $100m appears in the partnership's books. It appears again inside the holding company's investment in the partnership, and again inside the trust's investment in the holding company. Three sets of books, one fund interest. The trust's real share of it is 40% of 60%, which is 24%, or $24m.

Do that across four trusts, a holding company, a partnership, six asset vehicles and a co-investment vehicle, and you get the reference household below: $12.01bn of legal books and $1.50bn actually owned.

![A look-through consolidation showing legal books of $12.01bn against a consolidated $1.50bn, with a per-asset table giving legal owner, asset class, valuation basis, effective ownership, gross value and attributed value.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/look-through-consolidation.a6726248.jpg)

**Every row carries its effective ownership.** Forty percent of a $157.5m holding company is $63.0m. The percentage comes from the capital accounts, and the attributed value follows from it.

## Effective ownership comes from the capital accounts

In many family offices the ownership percentages live in a spreadsheet, keyed in by hand and updated when someone remembers to. It goes stale the first time a trust makes a distribution or one sibling buys part of another's interest.

Here, ownership weights are derived from capital holdings. When capital moves, the effective ownership moves with it, and so do the consolidation, the structure chart and the income allocations. They all read the same numbers.

## When one vehicle has several owners

Family structures are rarely clean trees. Two trusts can both own the holding company. A co-investment vehicle can be owned by the partnership and by an individual directly. Drawn as separate trees, a shared vehicle repeats on every branch and its value gets counted twice in any total built from the drawing.

The structure is kept as a graph instead: every vehicle appears once, with all of its owners converging on it. Allocations follow the same graph, so income on a shared vehicle is split among its owners in proportion to their capital and then carried up each owner's chain.

![An ownership structure drawn as a flow diagram: four family trusts converging on a holding company of $3.58bn, through a family partnership, out to six asset sleeves and a co-investment vehicle.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/structure-flow.49a61406.jpg)

**Value passing through each vehicle.** Band width is the value flowing through, so the holding company shows both its $157.5m in its own legal books and the $3.58bn it controls.

## What the consolidated view carries

Each asset row shows its legal owner, asset class, valuation basis, effective ownership, gross value and attributed value. Fund interests carry the as-of date of the manager's last statement, and company marks carry their valuation method. A fund still held at last quarter's statement shows that date on its row.

From there the net worth view groups value by category, by holder and by period, with the movement between periods. Exposure and concentration read from the same attributed values, so a family's concentration in one sector is measured on the family's attributed share of each holding.

## Where this connects

The family's private fund interests can be looked through a second time, from each fund to the companies it holds, using manager-supplied holdings. That view is covered under [fund of funds accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/). The household's accounting, trusts and reporting packs are covered under [family office accounting](https://1494labs.com/family-office-accounting/).

## Related reading

- [Family office accounting](https://1494labs.com/family-office-accounting/)

- [Fund of funds accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/)

- [Liquidity forecasting and commitment pacing](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/)

- [Capabilities and status](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/)

# Fund Accounting API and AI

For fund managers, allocators and administrators connecting their book to other systems and AI assistants.

## Accounting Records and Notice Endpoints

- Capital call notices are available as PDFs through the API. The notice carries the investor's amount, due date and wire instructions from approved bank details, for the accounting team's call-notice process.

- Distribution notices are available as PDFs through the API. Each notice belongs to a recorded distribution and provides the investor-facing document for that cash event.

- Journal Entries shows the postings created by accounting transactions. Each journal entry retains its source type and source identifier. The entry detail displays the accounting lines and the recorded transaction source.

- Investor statements show opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expenses, fees and ending capital. The statement draws these amounts from the investor's recorded account and the fund's reporting period.

## Terms

Public API refers to programmatic access to accounting records. MCP connects AI assistants to tools and data. The accounting endpoints listed here cover notice PDFs, journal sources and investor statements.

## Questions

### Can I retrieve a capital call notice through the API?

Yes. The capital call notice endpoint returns a PDF with the investor's amount, due date and wire instructions. Wire instructions come from approved bank details. The notice is retrieved through the API.

### Can I retrieve an investor distribution notice?

Yes. The distribution notice endpoint returns the PDF for a recorded distribution. It provides the investor-facing notice for that distribution through the API.

### Can I identify the transaction behind a journal entry?

Yes. Each journal entry records a source type and source identifier. Journal Entries displays the posting detail and source label; underlying distribution entries also have a direct link to the source transaction.

### Can an investor statement show flows, fees and ending capital?

Yes. The capital account statement includes opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expense, fees and ending capital. It records the period's movement for the investor account and its closing balance.

# Fund, Partnership and Investor Accounting

For fund managers, allocators and fund administrators.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Create a fund with legal entity, vintage, term, currency, fiscal year

- Share classes or units with different fee terms

- Management fee terms with rate, basis, step-downs, offsets

- Carried interest and waterfall terms with hurdle, catch-up, tiers, European or American

- Chart of accounts per fund, with a default template

- Onboard an investor with unique ID, legal name, tax details, type

- Bank account details on the investor record for inbound and outbound cash

- Generate call notices per investor with amounts, due date, wire instructions

- Distribution notices per investor

- Unfunded commitment tracking per investor and per fund

- Mark a position to a valuation with an effective date and a source

- Calculate management fees for a period from the fee terms

- Journal entries posted from every transaction type, traceable to the source transaction

- Period open, close, lock, and reopen with an audit trail

- Close checklist and reviewer sign-off gating lock

- NAV calculation per fund and per share class at period end

- Capital accounts per investor that tie to the general ledger

- Allocation of income, expense, gains across investors by ownership, multi-level up the chain

- Trial balance per fund and period, frozen at close

- Financial statements for one fund and period (income, balance, changes in net assets, cash flow)

- Investor capital account statement (beginning, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expense, fees, ending)

- Report packs by persona, assembled and exportable as one document

- In-product support requests raised from a screen and tracked

- Generate investor statements for all accounts, review, publish and resend

## Related Notes

- [What an opening balance has to carry](https://1494labs.com/notes/what-an-opening-balance-has-to-carry/)

- [ABOR and IBOR](https://1494labs.com/notes/abor-and-ibor/)

- [Management fee offsets](https://1494labs.com/notes/management-fee-offsets/)

## Questions

### Can I strike NAV for the fund and its share classes?

Yes. The NAV workflow supports preliminary and final strikes and restatements. Saved NAV versions include share-class lines, and the share register shows the class results for the fund's strike.

### Do investor capital accounts tie to general ledger capital?

Yes. The accounting checks compare investor capital balances with the fund's general ledger capital. Capital Accounts displays the investor balances. The tie is an accounting invariant checked across the book.

### Can a closed period be reopened with a recorded reason?

Yes. Period Close supports a governed reopen action for users with reopen permission. The reason is recorded with the event, and the period history retains the closing, locking and reopening actions.

### Can an investor statement show flows, fees and ending capital?

Yes. The capital account statement includes opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expense, fees and ending capital. It records the period's movement for the investor account and its closing balance.

### Can I review investor statements before publishing a run?

Yes. Statement runs group generation, review and publication. Each account has its own result, allowing the team to inspect a failed item and review the generated statements before publishing the run.

# 1494 Labs and an outsourced fund administrator

Compare the accounting system with the service relationship, and decide which book and reconciliation your team needs to own.

Updated November 3, 2026

## Separate the service decision from the book

A fund administrator provides people and contracted services. Fund accounting software provides the system in which a team keeps and reviews the book. Scope the work first: who books transactions, calculates NAV, reviews allocations, produces investor reports and approves the close?

1494 Labs is fund accounting software for fund teams and administrators. A software demonstration should prove the accounting workflow; a service evaluation should establish responsibility, staffing, reporting deadlines and review arrangements.

## Three workflows to evaluate

- **An internal book.** Your team runs the ledger and close. Confirm that you have the people and review process for the work you retain.

- **A shadow book.** Your team maintains an independent record and compares it with the administrator's reports. Agree the data exchange, timing and break resolution.

- **An administrator-operated book.** Ask what access, exports and supporting records your team receives, and who approves adjustments.

## Test the handoff with one period

1. List the inputs each party supplies and their delivery dates.

2. Reconcile investment positions, cash and opening investor capital.

3. Compare the fee and allocation calculations under the same agreement terms.

4. Record each difference with its source, owner and resolution.

5. Agree which reports are approved and how corrections reach both teams.

1494 Labs includes shadow reconciliation for comparing an outside administrator's book with your own. Ask to see a break identified and traced to its source. For an administrator evaluating the platform, ask to see the workflow across several client funds.

Bring the proposed division of responsibilities to a [demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact). Review [fund administration workflows](https://1494labs.com/fund-administration-software/) and the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) before agreeing the scope.


---

Source: https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-software-vs-spreadsheets/

# 1494 Labs vs spreadsheets for fund accounting

Compare a spreadsheet-based fund close with a ledger that traces fees, allocations and investor balances to their entries.

Updated November 3, 2026

## Compare the work of closing a period

A useful evaluation starts with one completed period from a fund like yours. Reproduce the fee, allocation and investor statement, then change one input and follow its effect through the book.

| Controller's task | Spreadsheet workflow to inspect | 1494 Labs demonstration to request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Update a fund's fee terms | Locate the formulas and copies that depend on the term | Show the configured fee terms and the resulting calculation |
| Explain an investor balance | Trace workbook references to ledger exports | Trace the capital account to allocations and entries |
| Check the close | Review reconciliations and exception tabs | Show the checks and investigate an exception |
| Prepare the next period | Verify copied formulas, opening balances and fee state | Show the next period's opening state and calculation trail |

## Use a worked acceptance test

1. Agree the opening ledger, investor balances and fee state.

2. Run the period with the same dated transactions and terms.

3. Reconcile NAV, fees and every investor's closing balance.

4. Introduce a corrected input and inspect the affected entries and reports.

5. Save the evidence and agree who owns the accepted book.

The objective is a reproducible close. Keep independent spreadsheet checks where they help a reviewer, and make the accounting record and approval process clear.

1494 Labs supports configured fees, allocations and waterfalls with a traceable ledger and recurring checks. The [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) identifies current scope and planned work. [Read the conversion checklist](https://1494labs.com/notes/moving-a-fund-off-spreadsheets/), then [request a demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact) using reference funds shaped like your own.

# Fund Administration Software

For fund administrators accounting for many funds with different terms.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Create a fund with legal entity, vintage, term, currency, fiscal year

- Share classes or units with different fee terms

- Management fee terms with rate, basis, step-downs, offsets

- Carried interest and waterfall terms with hurdle, catch-up, tiers, European or American

- Chart of accounts per fund, with a default template

- Onboard an investor with unique ID, legal name, tax details, type

- Bank account details on the investor record for inbound and outbound cash

- Generate call notices per investor with amounts, due date, wire instructions

- Distribution notices per investor

- Unfunded commitment tracking per investor and per fund

- Mark a position to a valuation with an effective date and a source

- Calculate management fees for a period from the fee terms

- Journal entries posted from every transaction type, traceable to the source transaction

- Period open, close, lock, and reopen with an audit trail

- Close checklist and reviewer sign-off gating lock

- NAV calculation per fund and per share class at period end

- Capital accounts per investor that tie to the general ledger

- Allocation of income, expense, gains across investors by ownership, multi-level up the chain

- Trial balance per fund and period, frozen at close

- Financial statements for one fund and period (income, balance, changes in net assets, cash flow)

- Investor capital account statement (beginning, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expense, fees, ending)

- Report packs by persona, assembled and exportable as one document

- In-product support requests raised from a screen and tracked

- Generate investor statements for all accounts, review, publish and resend

## Related Notes

- [Converting from a fund administrator](https://1494labs.com/notes/converting-from-a-fund-administrator/)

- [What an opening balance has to carry](https://1494labs.com/notes/what-an-opening-balance-has-to-carry/)

- [Checking the book against outside records](https://1494labs.com/notes/a-wrong-number-that-agrees-with-itself/)

## Questions

### Can investors in one fund have different fee terms?

Yes. Unitized funds use share classes, and capital-based funds use fee classes. The Share Classes and Fee Terms screens record these groups and their terms within the fund.

### Can a calculated management fee post to the books?

Yes. After fee terms are configured, Fees calculates the period accrual and provides posting and reversal actions. The posted accrual records the management fee in the fund's accounting books.

### Can reviewer sign-off gate the period lock?

Yes. The close checklist and review events are recorded for the period. Locking checks that the required sign-off is present, and the reviewer's action remains in the period history.

### Can I retrieve the trial balance frozen at close?

Yes. Reporting includes frozen trial balances and revisions. The frozen balance keeps the ledger totals frozen at the close, so a reviewer can inspect the recorded close and the revisions attached to it.

### Can I review investor statements before publishing a run?

Yes. Statement runs group generation, review and publication. Each account has its own result, allowing the team to inspect a failed item and review the generated statements before publishing the run.

## Product Screens

![A Statement of Changes in Partners' Capital, from beginning capital through contributions, net income and fees to ending capital.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/statement-of-changes.39e06e66.jpg)

**Ending capital ties to the dashboard NAV to the cent.** Both figures come from the same ledger, so no reconciliation runs between them.

![A fee gross-to-net statement: five management fee accruals, each from gross accrual to net fee, totaling $65,934.06 gross and net with no offsets, waivers or rebates.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/fee-gross-to-net.a19c17c9.jpg)

**Gross to net, per accrual, per client.** Each posted fee keeps the steps it was calculated with, in order (gross, then offsets, waivers and rebates, then net), saved when it posted, so a later change to the terms does not rewrite it.

![An exception detail panel for the operating cash account at 2026-06-30: the bank statement's closing balance of $747,850.00 against the book's $750,000.00, a difference of $2,150.00, a reason field, and buttons to acknowledge, resolve or accept the difference.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/break-detail.dc783d42.jpg)

**Expected, actual, difference, and a decision with a name on it.**
Resolve and accept are deliberately different: resolved means the
numbers now agree, accepted means they still differ and somebody decided
that is correct. Accepting requires a note, because "they differ and
that is fine" is only institutional memory if it says why.

![A cash movements blotter of settled movements: investments into underlying managers, investor subscriptions, and transfers between the fund's own cash accounts, each with its source and counterparty.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/cash-movements.61bcbb09.jpg)

**Cash movements, with their sources.** Select many rows and act on them together in every table, because an administrator's day is spent on many rows at once.

![The exceptions worklist: two open exceptions on the operating cash account, raised by an imported bank statement. The closing balance differs from the book by $2,150.00, and one statement line of -$2,150.00 matches nothing in the book.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/reconciliation-breaks.3b91eb16.jpg)

**A finding has somewhere to go.**
An imported bank statement matched every line but one, a $2,150 fee
the book never recorded, and raised two exceptions: the balance and the unmatched line. An exception ages, gets assigned, and keeps what was decided
about it, so next month's exception on the same account arrives with
last month's reasoning attached.

# Fund and Investor Reporting

For fund managers, allocators and administrators preparing NAV and investor reporting.

## Accounting Capabilities

- NAV records preliminary, final and restated fund values, including share-class lines. The NAV and period-close screens show the fund's strike workflow, with class results available through the share register.

- Capital Accounts shows investor balances for the selected fund. Accounting checks compare investor capital snapshots with general ledger capital, giving the investor balances a defined tie to the fund's capital accounts.

- Reporting provides the trial balance for the fund, including the balance frozen at close and its revisions. The frozen balance preserves the ledger totals used for that close and subsequent review.

- Fund Statements provides an income statement, balance sheet, statement of changes in net assets and cash-flow statement for one fund and period. The reporting screen uses the selected fund and reporting period.

- Investor statements show opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expenses, fees and ending capital. The statement draws these amounts from the investor's recorded account and the fund's reporting period.

- Reporting includes report packs organized by audience. A pack runs for its fund and period and can be exported as PDF or CSV, collecting the selected reports for the intended recipient.

- Reporting groups investor statement production into runs. The team generates, reviews and publishes the statements, with failures recorded per account so an individual statement failure is isolated within the run.

## Related Notes

- [Which columns can be added](https://1494labs.com/notes/which-columns-can-be-added/)

- [ABOR and IBOR](https://1494labs.com/notes/abor-and-ibor/)

## Questions

### Can I prepare the financial statements for one fund and period?

Yes. Fund Statements includes the income statement, balance sheet, statement of changes in net assets and cash-flow statement. These reports use one fund and reporting period for the financial statement set.

### Can an investor statement show flows, fees and ending capital?

Yes. The capital account statement includes opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expense, fees and ending capital. It records the period's movement for the investor account and its closing balance.

### Can I assemble a report pack for a particular audience?

Yes. Report packs are organized by audience and run for a specified fund and period. Pack results can be exported as PDF or CSV for the recipient's reporting process.

### Can I strike NAV for the fund and its share classes?

Yes. The NAV workflow supports preliminary and final strikes and restatements. Saved NAV versions include share-class lines, and the share register shows the class results for the fund's strike.

### Can I review investor statements before publishing a run?

Yes. Statement runs group generation, review and publication. Each account has its own result, allowing the team to inspect a failed item and review the generated statements before publishing the run.

# Fund of funds accounting, from the manager's statement to the company underneath

A fund of funds keeps its books on numbers someone else produces. Each underlying manager reports when it chooses, in whatever format it uses, and sometimes revises what it sent last quarter. The accounting has to hold those numbers with their dates attached, take corrections without breaking what was already reported, and still answer the question investors ask most: what do we actually own?

Fund of funds · roughly 5 minutes

## Every mark carries its date

Each underlying fund position carries a cost basis, an unrealized gain and the date it was last valued. A manager's NAV statement is recorded with its as-of date and its source. When the quarter closes and one manager hasn't reported, the position shows the date of the mark it is still carried at.

![Portfolio holdings for a fund of funds: six named underlying managers, each with cost, value, the date it was last valued and a link to its marks.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/portfolio-holdings.3916f10a.jpg)

**Six managers, each at cost and at value.** The date each was last revalued sits on the row, because the age of an input is part of the number.

## Late statements are corrections

Managers often send an estimate and then a final. The true-up is recorded as a correction with its own record, and a closed period can be corrected without disturbing what was already reported for it. Position performance (IRR, TVPI, DPI and RVPI) restates with the corrected mark.

## Looking through to the companies

Underlying holdings come in by CSV import from the managers' reports. Look-through then shows the companies behind each fund interest, grouped by sector and geography, as of any date you choose. Where two of your managers hold the same company, it appears once with both paths into it.

Your share of an underlying fund's holdings needs the fund's total size, which only the manager can report. When a manager doesn't report it, that share is left out and the view states why. A guessed percentage would be worse than a stated gap. Holdings without a linked company classification show a blank classification, so you can find and fix them.

Look-through runs on both ownership bases, and the results export as CSV.

## Commitments and the cash they will need

Unfunded commitments are shown by investor and by underlying fund. A fund-level setting chooses whether unfunded is measured at historical or spot rates, so the figure follows the basis the fund reports on. [Commitment pacing and liquidity forecasting](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/) projects the calls those commitments will make against cash and undrawn credit.

## Your own investors

The fund of funds has investors of its own. Management fees are calculated from the fund's saved terms and posted as accruals that can be reversed. Investor statements show opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expenses, fees and ending capital. If the fund draws capital from its own LPs, calls and distributions follow the same [capital call and distribution](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/) workflow as any drawdown fund.

## Related reading

- [Family office accounting](https://1494labs.com/family-office-accounting/), for families with large private fund programs

- [Endowment and foundation investment accounting](https://1494labs.com/endowment-foundation-accounting/)

- [Liquidity forecasting and commitment pacing](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/)

- [Capital calls and distributions](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/)

- [Capabilities and status](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/)

# Fund Accounting Glossary

Terms for fund managers, allocators and administrators reviewing investor capital, structures and portfolio cash flows.

## Blocker

A corporation held between investors and investments, with tax accounted for at that entity.

[Blocker Corporation Accounting](https://1494labs.com/blocker-corporation-accounting/)

## AIV

An alternative investment vehicle used alongside a fund to hold an investment.

[Holding Company and Family Office Entity Accounting](https://1494labs.com/holding-company-and-family-office-entity-accounting/)

## SPV

A special purpose vehicle formed to hold a particular investment or group of investments.

[Holding Company and Family Office Entity Accounting](https://1494labs.com/holding-company-and-family-office-entity-accounting/)

## Holdco

A holding company that owns interests in other entities.

[Holding Company and Family Office Entity Accounting](https://1494labs.com/holding-company-and-family-office-entity-accounting/)

## Strip sale

A sale of LP interests across several underlying funds in one transaction.

[Secondaries and Strip Sale Accounting](https://1494labs.com/secondaries-and-strip-sale-accounting/)

## Continuation vehicle

A vehicle that acquires investments from an existing fund in a GP-led secondary transaction.

[Secondaries for Fund of Funds](https://1494labs.com/secondaries-for-fund-of-funds/)

## Equalization

An investor-level adjustment used to allocate incentive fees when investors subscribe at different values.

[Equalization and Series Accounting](https://1494labs.com/equalization-and-series-accounting/)

## Series accounting

Separate subscription series used to track investor entry values and fee calculations.

[Equalization and Series Accounting](https://1494labs.com/equalization-and-series-accounting/)

## High-water mark

The value an investor must recover before further performance becomes subject to an incentive fee under the agreed terms.

[Equalization and Series Accounting](https://1494labs.com/equalization-and-series-accounting/)

## Crystallization

The point when an accrued incentive fee becomes payable under the fund terms.

[Equalization and Series Accounting](https://1494labs.com/equalization-and-series-accounting/)

## Side pocket

An investment pool with participation accounted for separately from the main dealing pool.

[Side Pocket Accounting](https://1494labs.com/side-pocket-accounting/)

## Look-through

A view of the holdings behind an investment in another fund or entity.

[Fund of Funds Accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/)

## Recallable capital

Distributed capital that the fund may call again under its agreement.

[Capital Call and Distribution Software](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/)

## Unfunded commitment

The remaining amount an investor has committed and may still be called to contribute.

[Capital Call and Distribution Software](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/)

## Commitment pacing

Planning the timing and size of commitments to underlying funds.

[Liquidity Forecasting and Commitment Pacing](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/)

## Clawback

A requirement to return excess carry under the terms of the fund agreement.

[Waterfall and Carried Interest Accounting](https://1494labs.com/waterfall-and-carried-interest-accounting/)

## Hurdle

A return threshold used in calculating carried interest or incentive fees.

[Waterfall and Carried Interest Accounting](https://1494labs.com/waterfall-and-carried-interest-accounting/)

## Catch-up

A waterfall tier that allocates proceeds to bring the carry recipient to the agreed share.

[Waterfall and Carried Interest Accounting](https://1494labs.com/waterfall-and-carried-interest-accounting/)

## ILPA notice

A capital call or distribution notice using the applicable ILPA reporting format.

[Capital Call and Distribution Software](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/)
