# Which columns can be added, and which cannot

A subtotal that is wrong looks exactly like a subtotal that is right. Every
reporting tool will happily add a column of percentages, and the resulting number is meaningless.

Reporting · roughly 5 minutes

## Four classes, three behaviors

Whether a column can be aggregated is a property of the column itself, whatever grid it sits in. The same table routinely contains columns from
three of these classes at once.

| Class | Examples | Across entities, one date | Across dates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Flows** | Contributions, distributions, fees charged, realized gains | Add | Add |
| **Point-in-time balances** | NAV, cash, unfunded commitment, position value | Add | **Never** |
| **Rates and per-unit values** | NAV per share, price, fee rate, ownership percentage | **Never** | **Never** |
| **Derived statistics** | IRR, time-weighted return, volatility, Sharpe | Recomputed from the combined series | |

A grid of capital accounts will carry contributions, a closing balance and
an ownership percentage side by side. One of those three sums down the
page, one sums across entities but not across periods, and one never sums at
all. A tool that treats a column as a column gets two of them wrong.

![Subscriptions grouped by investor. Six investors each show a summed subtotal that foots to the $20,600,000 total, and one group is expanded to its three subscriptions with date, account, amount and posted status.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/grid-grouped-subtotals.314567a9.jpg)

**Grouped in place, with the rows still underneath.**
Subscriptions grouped by investor. The six subtotals foot to the $20,600,000 total above them, and the expanded group shows the three subscriptions that produce $4,800,000. Amount is a flow, so it sums; had a rate or a percentage been
on this grid it would have gone blank at the group level.

## An average of averages, in money

A fund has two share classes. Class A holds $80m at a 1.0% management fee;
Class B holds $20m at 2.0%. What is the fund's management fee rate?

| Method | Rate | Implied annual fee on $100m |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Average of the two class rates | 1.50% | $1,500,000 |
| Weighted by the capital each rate applies to | 1.20% | $1,200,000 |

$300,000 a year, and the wrong figure is the one a grid produces by default,
because averaging is what a column of percentages invites. The error also
moves with the mix, so it cannot be spotted as a constant bias: rebalance
the classes and the gap changes size without anything on screen changing
appearance.

The same trap sits one level deeper. A weighted average computed at a
subtotal must run over the individual rows beneath it. Averaging subtotals that are themselves averages compounds the
error at every level, and a deep grouping tree can be wrong by a great deal
more than this example.

## The denominator that should not move

A holdings grid shows each position as a percentage of fund NAV. The fund is
$100m: $60m of equities, $40m of credit. Group the grid by asset class and
the percentage column has to decide what it is a percentage of.

| | Equities | Credit | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Denominator stays fund NAV | 60% | 40% | 100% |
| Denominator becomes the group | 100% | 100% | 200% |

The second row is what a grid does if the percentage is treated as an
ordinary computed column, and it is worth noticing that it does not look
broken. Each group reads 100%, which is a plausible thing for a group to
read. Only the total gives it away, and totals of percentage columns are
frequently hidden precisely because they look odd.

For this to work the grid has to know that the denominator is external to
the rows on screen. That is a different kind of thing from a column of values, and most
reporting tools have nowhere to put it.

## Balances do not sum across time

Group a capital-account grid by month and the closing balance column will
offer a total. Twelve monthly NAVs added together is twelve times the
average NAV, a number with no referent: the fund never held it, and it is
not a cash flow either.

Contributions in the next column over do sum across those same twelve
months, correctly, because a flow is a quantity of money that moved. So the rule has to attach to the column itself.
A balance column under a date grouping should go blank at and above the date
level, while the flow column beside it keeps totaling.

## Statistics have no shortcut

A group's volatility is the volatility of the group's composite return
series. Averaging the members' volatilities gets it
wrong under any weighting, because the members' returns are correlated and the statistic
depends on that correlation. The same holds for Sharpe, beta and tracking
error. A group's IRR is the IRR of the combined cash flow stream, so it needs the members' cash flows themselves.

So the honest answer at a subtotal is either the recomputed statistic or
nothing. If the composite series has not been built, there is no correct
number available, and any figure in that cell is invented.

## Blank, with a reason, is an answer

An empty cell looks like something failed. A computed cell that should
have been empty looks like it worked. The second one is the expensive
mistake, and it is the one that reaches an investor, because nothing about
it invites a second look.

A cell that cannot be computed honestly should say so, and say why: no
composite series, denominator not resolvable at this level, not additive
across dates. That turns a silent wrong answer into a visible limitation,
which is a thing a controller can work with.

## What to check

- ✓**Can you total a NAV-per-share column?**
If the tool permits it, someone will do it eventually, and the first time
it matters will be in front of somebody's investor.

- ✓**Under grouping, does a percentage keep its denominator?**
Group a holdings view by anything and look at the total.

- ✓**Does a balance column blank out on a date axis**
while the flow column beside it keeps summing?

- ✓**What appears when a subtotal cannot be computed?**
A zero is the worst possible answer, because zero is a value.

- ✓**What survives an export?**
Every one of these rules is enforced by the grid. A spreadsheet has no
idea which column is which, and will add all of them on request. If the
analysis only exists after an export, none of this protects it.

- [A wrong number that agrees with itself](https://1494labs.com/notes/a-wrong-number-that-agrees-with-itself/), when the total ties and is still wrong

- [ABOR and IBOR](https://1494labs.com/notes/abor-and-ibor/), two books that group the same positions differently

- [For administrators](https://1494labs.com/fund-administration-software/), many clients on one platform

- [Statements and reporting](https://docs.1494labs.com/guide/statements-and-reporting/) in the product docs

- [All notes](https://1494labs.com/notes/)

## How we handle it

In 1494 Labs each column carries its own rule for how it adds up, each
percentage keeps its denominator through any grouping, and a subtotal that cannot be computed honestly renders blank with its reason. A saved analysis has its own address, so the cut a controller builds on
screen can also be pulled by another system through the API, with the
rules still applied.

[Request a demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact)

# Portfolio Accounting Across Asset Classes

For fund managers, allocators and administrators accounting for multi-asset portfolios.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Valuations records dated marks for underlying fund interests, portfolio companies and priced instruments. The entry fields follow the asset: fund NAV statements carry an as-of date and source; company marks carry a valuation method and memo.

- Fund Statements provides an income statement, balance sheet, statement of changes in net assets and cash-flow statement for one fund and period. The reporting screen uses the selected fund and reporting period.

- Investor statements show opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expenses, fees and ending capital. The statement draws these amounts from the investor's recorded account and the fund's reporting period.

- Reporting includes report packs organized by audience. A pack runs for its fund and period and can be exported as PDF or CSV, collecting the selected reports for the intended recipient.

- The company Exit screen calculates whole-holding exit proceeds through liquidation preferences, participation and caps. The calculation uses the company's capital structure to allocate the exit value across the security classes.

- The company valuation screen records a dated mark up or down. The company's valuation method and memo stay with the mark, giving quarter-end company valuation records a date and stated calculation approach.

- Underlying fund positions carry manager-reported marks and performance. Valuations and Look-through show position IRR, TVPI, DPI and RVPI, with support for late manager statements and the resulting restatement of reported values.

- Look-through shows the underlying company holdings behind fund investments. It supports as-of views, shared ownership subtrees and CSV export. Company holdings supplied by import become part of the portfolio's underlying exposure view.

## Related Notes

- [ABOR and IBOR](https://1494labs.com/notes/abor-and-ibor/)

- [Which columns can be added](https://1494labs.com/notes/which-columns-can-be-added/)

## Questions

### Can I record dated marks for different investment types?

Yes. Valuations supports underlying fund NAV statements, portfolio company valuations and instrument prices. Fund statements record their as-of date and source. Company valuations record the valuation date, method and memo.

### Can a company exit calculation include liquidation preferences?

Yes. Company exit waterfalls calculate proceeds using liquidation preferences, participation and caps. The supported exit action covers the whole holding and allocates the exit value across the company's security classes.

### Can I record late manager marks and underlying-fund performance?

Yes. Underlying fund positions retain manager marks and position performance, including IRR, TVPI, DPI and RVPI. The valuation process supports late quarter statements and restatement of the affected reported values.

### Can I look through fund investments to the underlying companies?

Yes. Look-through presents company holdings behind underlying funds, including shared ownership subtrees and as-of views. Underlying holdings arrive by CSV import, and the look-through results can be exported as CSV.

### Can I prepare the financial statements for one fund and period?

Yes. Fund Statements includes the income statement, balance sheet, statement of changes in net assets and cash-flow statement. These reports use one fund and reporting period for the financial statement set.

## Related Accounting Pages

- [Fund of Funds Accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/)

# Portfolio Company KPI Collection

For private equity and venture finance teams collecting company financials and reporting valuations.

## Company Financials and KPIs

- Company Financials & KPIs provides templates for revenue, EBITDA, net debt and custom KPIs. The team can upload a completed template or create a secure submission link for the company. Accepted figures appear beside the company valuation mark, with the submission used recorded.

- The template includes the reporting date and all required metrics. Upload checks cover the expected columns, missing fields, valid dates, duplicate dates and finite numeric values. Revenue, EBITDA and net debt use the company's currency; custom KPIs retain their agreed units.

- Each submission and correction retains its date, currency, source and submitter. The collection history preserves earlier evidence. Operator review accepts or rejects an external submission with a recorded reason.

- The valuation screen shows the collected figures beside the mark and records the financial submission selected for that valuation. Fund report sections include company financials and KPIs and flag companies with missing reports.

## Supporting Accounting

- Valuations records dated marks for underlying fund interests, portfolio companies and priced instruments. The entry fields follow the asset: fund NAV statements carry an as-of date and source; company marks carry a valuation method and memo.

- Fund Statements provides an income statement, balance sheet, statement of changes in net assets and cash-flow statement for one fund and period. The reporting screen uses the selected fund and reporting period.

- The company Exit screen calculates whole-holding exit proceeds through liquidation preferences, participation and caps. The calculation uses the company's capital structure to allocate the exit value across the security classes.

- The company valuation screen records a dated mark up or down. The company's valuation method and memo stay with the mark, giving quarter-end company valuation records a date and stated calculation approach.

## Terms

Company financials include revenue, EBITDA and net debt. KPIs are the additional operating measures defined in each company template. Reporting dates and company currency stay with the submitted figures.

## Questions

### Can a company submit its financials through a secure link?

Yes. An operator creates a company-specific submission link. The company downloads its collection template and uploads the completed figures. External submissions wait for operator acceptance before they become reporting or valuation evidence.

### Can I define the KPIs each company reports?

Yes. The company template contains revenue, EBITDA and net debt plus the custom metrics the team defines. The downloaded template includes the required reporting-date column and metric fields. Custom KPIs use the agreed units.

### Are dates and numbers checked when a file is uploaded?

Yes. Upload validation checks template columns, required fields, reporting dates, duplicate dates and numeric values. It rejects invalid or non-finite numbers. Currency and the reporting date remain with the accepted figures.

### Can I see the figures used beside a valuation mark?

Yes. The company valuation screen presents the collected financial figures beside the mark and records the submission selected as evidence. Submission history retains earlier uploads and corrections with their reporting date, source and submitter.

### Can fund reporting identify missing company financials?

Yes. The company financials section in fund reporting includes collected company metrics and identifies companies with missing reports. External submissions become available as evidence after an operator accepts them.

# Private Equity Fund Accounting

For private equity managers and administrators running drawdown funds.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Fund setup records the legal entity, base currency and fiscal year. Closed-end funds also carry vintage, fund term, extension dates and hard cap, so the fund record contains the terms used by the accounting team.

- Waterfall setup records the hurdle, catch-up and distribution tiers for European or American carry arrangements. A policy preview shows the configured waterfall before it is used for the fund.

- Capital call notices are available as PDFs through the API. The notice carries the investor's amount, due date and wire instructions from approved bank details, for the accounting team's call-notice process.

- Distribution notices are available as PDFs through the API. Each notice belongs to a recorded distribution and provides the investor-facing document for that cash event.

- Capital Accounts shows unfunded commitments by investor and fund. A fund setting chooses the historical or spot measure, so the reported unfunded amount follows the accounting basis selected for that fund.

- The Fees screen calculates period management fees from the fund's saved terms. Accruals can be posted and reversed, giving the period fee a corresponding accounting entry in the fund's books.

- Capital Accounts shows investor balances for the selected fund. Accounting checks compare investor capital snapshots with general ledger capital, giving the investor balances a defined tie to the fund's capital accounts.

- Investor statements show opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expenses, fees and ending capital. The statement draws these amounts from the investor's recorded account and the fund's reporting period.

- The company Exit screen calculates whole-holding exit proceeds through liquidation preferences, participation and caps. The calculation uses the company's capital structure to allocate the exit value across the security classes.

- The company valuation screen records a dated mark up or down. The company's valuation method and memo stay with the mark, giving quarter-end company valuation records a date and stated calculation approach.

## Related Notes

## Questions

### Can I record a closed-end fund's vintage and term?

Yes. Fund setup includes vintage, investment term, extension dates and hard cap for closed-end funds, alongside the legal entity, currency and fiscal year. These fields belong to the fund record.

### Can I configure European and American waterfall terms?

Yes. Waterfall setup supports European and American policies, with hurdle, catch-up and tier terms. The policy preview calculates the configured distribution sequence so the finance team can review the terms.

### Can a company exit calculation include liquidation preferences?

Yes. Company exit waterfalls calculate proceeds using liquidation preferences, participation and caps. The supported exit action covers the whole holding and allocates the exit value across the company's security classes.

### Can I record a quarter-end portfolio company valuation?

Yes. The company valuation screen records a valuation date, method and memo with the mark. It supports company marks up or down for the reporting date being recorded.

### Can I see unfunded commitments by investor?

Yes. Capital Accounts reports unfunded commitments per investor and per fund. The fund's setting selects the historical or spot measure used in that view, giving the team a defined basis for the outstanding amount.

# Real estate fund accounting, down to the lease

A real estate fund has two sets of numbers that have to agree. The fund's ledger, where investors' capital and the promote live. And the properties underneath it, where rent is billed, leases are amended and operating expenses come in. When the second set sits in a property system and is re-keyed into the first, the gap between them is where the close slows down.

Real estate · roughly 6 minutes

## Leases and the rent roll

A lease records the tenant, the unit and its area, the term, and a base rent schedule with its escalations: fixed steps, steps indexed to inflation with a floor and a cap, and percentage rent over a sales breakpoint. Free-rent periods, security deposits and options sit on the lease too. Renewal, termination and purchase options are recorded as data and are accounted for only when someone exercises them, because whether an option is reasonably certain is a judgment the lease cannot make for you.

The rent roll can be produced as of any date, for one property or the whole fund. Each row carries the monthly and annualized base rent, rent per unit of area, months remaining, the deposit actually held and the straight-line receivable booked so far. Rent per area is blank, never zero, when the lease records no area.

## Straight-line rent, calculated from the lease

Under ASC 842, a lessor with free months and escalations recognizes rent on a straight-line basis, and the difference between rent recognized and rent billed builds up as a receivable. Here the schedule is calculated from the lease's terms, and the rent invoice and the journal entries follow from it, so the receivable always ties to the leases that produced it. Change a term and the affected periods restate; a period that is already closed does not move.

The reference fund holds an office lease of 12,000 square feet. It has three months of free rent, then 50,000 a month, stepping to 52,500 and then 55,000 on each anniversary. The total rent over the term is 1,740,000, recognized evenly over the 1,095 days of the lease.

One lease at 2026-06-30, after 18 monthly runs

| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Rent billed | 712,500.00 |
| Rent recognized, straight-line | 818,356.16 |
| Straight-line receivable | 105,856.16 |

The recognized figure is 1,740,000 times 515 elapsed days over 1,095, and the billed figure is what the free months and steps put on the invoices. The difference is the receivable, and it unwinds to zero by the end of the term.

Lease changes follow the standard. A modification takes effect from its date: the accrued receivable reduces the successor lease's payments, so it unwinds to zero by the new end date. When a lease ends early, the periods from the termination date restate. In the reference fund a lease ended on 20 March 2026: March's invoice was reissued for 20 days, 19,354.84, and the remaining receivable of 12,641.05 was written off against that lease. A tenant allowance and a leasing commission are amortized over the remaining term, the allowance against rental income and the commission to leasing cost. Improvements the landlord owns are depreciated over the shorter of their useful life and the remaining term.

## Each property keeps its own books

The property is a dimension on the journal lines, not a second ledger. Rent, recoveries, depreciation, mortgage interest and operating expenses all post to the property they belong to, and each building has an income statement and a balance sheet that read straight from the fund's ledger. The property figures, the fund-level lines that belong to no property and any other holdings add up to the fund's income statement over the same dates.

Two properties, one fund, 2025-01 to 2026-06

| Property | Rental revenue | Recoveries | Operating expenses | NOI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Office, 30,000 sq ft, mortgaged | 1,107,711.00 | 4,153.80 | 150,000.00 | 961,864.80 |
| Retail, 10,000 sq ft, unlevered | 648,122.74 | 0.00 | 57,000.00 | 591,122.74 |

Fund administration costs of 1,500 a month are attached to no building, so they stay at fund level and appear in neither NOI.

## Recoveries and the annual true-up

Common area maintenance, real estate tax and insurance are recovered through pools. A tenant's share can be its area over the building's, or a fixed percentage, with a base year or an expense stop where the lease has one. Monthly estimates are billed on the rent invoice. At year end the actual expense is read from the property's books and the reconciliation produces either an invoice for what the tenant owes or a credit for what the fund owes back, once per lease and year.

## NOI and the metrics investors ask for

NOI follows the usual definition, operating revenue less operating expenses, and is read from the same ledger as everything else. Physical occupancy is leased area over rentable area as of a date. Economic occupancy is billed fixed rent over gross potential fixed rent for a period. Weighted average lease term is shown by rent and by area, and rent per area comes with them. The areas and rents behind each ratio are carried beside it. A group total adds the facts first and divides afterward, so an occupancy figure for ten buildings is never an average of ten percentages. A ratio with nothing to divide by shows blank, with the reason.

## Valuation basis is a choice per fund

A fund elects how it carries its real property. On cost, which is the default, each building is carried at cost less depreciation, and appraisals are recorded as disclosure only. On fair value, the ASC 946 election for investment companies, there is no depreciation: the building is carried at its appraised value and the change runs through unrealized gain or loss. An appraisal records its approach (income capitalization, discounted cash flow or sales comparison) and the NOI it used. It is entered as preliminary and approved by a second person before it moves a value.

When a building is sold, the realized gain is net proceeds less carrying value. On a cost fund the quarter's depreciation runs first.

## The debt and the promote

A mortgage facility is tied to its property, so its draws, repayments and interest post to that building. Debt service coverage, loan-to-value and debt yield are derived per loan and per property from the facility's accruals, the property's NOI and its latest approved appraisal. With no approved appraisal, loan-to-value is blank rather than computed on book value. Covenant tests record a breach on the reconciliation worklist and block nothing. The promote runs through the [distribution waterfall](https://1494labs.com/distribution-waterfall-software/), deal by deal or whole-fund as the agreement says.

## What it doesn't do

Leases are held in the fund's base currency. Covenant tests inform; they do not stop a posting. Tax returns and K-1s stay with your tax preparer.

## Related reading

- [Distribution waterfall software](https://1494labs.com/distribution-waterfall-software/)

- [REIT accounting software](https://1494labs.com/reit-accounting-software/), for a REIT that holds these properties

- [Private equity fund accounting](https://1494labs.com/private-equity-fund-accounting/)

- [Capabilities and status](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/)

## Show us the portfolio

Tell us how many properties you hold and where the leases live today. We will walk you through a fund in the product, or stand up a sandbox with a reference real estate fund for you to work in.

[Request a demo](https://1494labs.com/?segment=other#contact)

# Registered fund accounting, from NAV strike to §19(a) notice

A registered fund answers to the SEC as well as its investors, and most of what it publishes has to be traceable to the book. A §19(a) notice has to say how much of a distribution came from income and how much was a return of capital. A repurchase offer has to prorate fairly when it is oversubscribed. A BDC has to know its asset coverage before it borrows or declares.

Registered funds · roughly 5 minutes

## NAV, struck by class

NAV is recorded as preliminary, final or restated, with a line for each share class. The share register shows the class results for each strike. Unitized funds hold their terms in share classes, and capital-based funds group investors with different fee terms into fee classes.

## A close you can show an examiner

Period close has a checklist and reviewer sign-off, and the period can't lock until the configured sign-off is recorded. Reopening a closed period needs permission and a recorded reason, and the period keeps its history of events. The trial balance is frozen at close, and any later revision is kept beside the frozen version, so a reviewer can see what the books said at close and what changed after.

![A fund trial balance by account with debit, credit and net columns, totaling $28,515,992.43 on each side with a net of $0.00.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/trial-balance.164f78ab.jpg)

**One fund's trial balance, tied.** Debits equal credits at the close, and the frozen balance stays beside any later revision.

## Distributions and the notices that describe them

§19(a) notices are sourced from the book, so the split between net investment income, capital gains and return of capital comes from the same ledger as the distribution itself. Managed distribution programs run on the same records.

## Repurchase offers

Repurchase offers are recorded with their terms, and an oversubscribed offer is prorated across tendering shareholders.

## BDC asset coverage

For a BDC, asset coverage is calculated from the book and applied as a gate, so the coverage test is part of the workflow instead of a separate spreadsheet check.

## Reporting

The income statement, balance sheet, statement of changes in net assets and cash-flow statement are produced for one fund and period. Report packs are organized by audience and export to PDF or CSV. Every figure traces back through the journal entry that posted it to the transaction that created it.

![A statement of changes for one fund and period: beginning capital, contributions, redemptions, distributions, net income and fees rolling to ending capital of $23,625,473.00.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/statement-of-changes.39e06e66.jpg)

**Beginning to ending, line by line.** The statement for one fund and period, from the same ledger as the rest.

## Related reading

- [ABOR and IBOR, and why most systems keep them apart](https://1494labs.com/notes/abor-and-ibor/)

- [Checking the book against outside records](https://1494labs.com/notes/a-wrong-number-that-agrees-with-itself/)

- [Fund administration software](https://1494labs.com/fund-administration-software/), for administrators running several registered funds

- [Capabilities and status](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/)

## Show us the fund

Tell us what you run, whether a RIC, a BDC or an interval fund, and we will walk you through a close in the product.

[Request a demo](https://1494labs.com/?segment=registered#contact)

# REIT accounting, with the qualification tests read from the book

A REIT keeps its status by passing tests every quarter and every year: what it owns, where its income comes from, how much it distributes and who owns its shares. Often those tests are computed in spreadsheets built from the general ledger after the fact. Here they recompute from the same books that produce the financial statements.

REITs · roughly 7 minutes

## Qualification, tracked as the year runs

The asset tests are measured at each quarter end: the 75% test for real estate assets, cash items and government securities, the limit on securities of taxable REIT subsidiaries, and the single-issuer and vote-or-value limits. The 75% and 95% income tests are measured year to date. Each ledger line is classified by a visible rule into rents from real property, mortgage interest, gains, dividends or TRS dividends, and the default rules can be edited. A line that no rule covers counts in the denominator and in no numerator, and is surfaced until someone classifies it.

The 90% distribution requirement is tested against REIT taxable income, which is either a figure your preparer supplies or one computed from the books. A dividend designated as a spillback for the prior year counts toward that year's test, and the 4% excise exposure on undistributed income is shown as information. At year end the ownership tests run: the 100-holder test, the five-or-fewer test, which looks through entity holders to the individuals behind them, and the 1% impermissible tenant service income test per property.

The tests flag and do not block. A failure raises a break on the reconciliation worklist, because what to do about it belongs to the REIT's management and its advisers.

## A quarter in which a test fails

The reference REIT holds one office building and earns fit-out management fees through a taxable REIT subsidiary, which pays them up as a dividend. A TRS dividend counts toward the 95% income test and not the 75% test. In the first quarter of 2025 that dominates the mix.

Reference REIT, 2025 tests

| Test | 2025-03-31 | 2025-06-30 | 2025-12-31 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 75% income, year to date | 61.93% fail | 76.48% pass | 86.79% pass |
| 95% income, year to date | 98.89% pass | 99.15% pass | 99.52% pass |
| 75% asset | 91.06% pass | 91.01% pass | 90.84% pass |
| TRS securities, 20% limit | 8.94% pass | 8.99% pass | 9.16% pass |

The first-quarter figure is 167,581.22 of qualifying income over 270,581.22 of gross income. The failure raises a break and the books carry on. Second-quarter rent restores the year-to-date ratio. A 750 line of sundry income that no rule covers is shown as unmapped rather than assumed to qualify.

At the 2025 year end the reference REIT has two shareholders, so the 100-holder test fails and says so, the five-or-fewer test is unresolved because both holders are in the top five and one is an organization, and the 1% service income test passes at 0.19%. An unresolved result states what the records would have to show to settle it.

## The operating partnership and OP units

In an UPREIT, the REIT owns most of an operating partnership and outside limited partners own the rest through OP units. The partnership is an ordinary fund in the product, with its own capital accounts, and the REIT's account in it is marked as the REIT's. Every other account is the noncontrolling interest. OP units are issued when a property is contributed, in kind, and the contribution records the property and its carryover tax basis. Units are redeemed for cash or exchanged for REIT shares. An exchange books the share issue at the units' carrying amount with no cash and no income, and the excess of fair value over carrying amount is a memorandum item.

The qualification tests look through to the partnership. The REIT is tested on its proportionate share of the partnership's assets and income, with the same classification, and the interest itself is dropped so nothing is counted twice. The noncontrolling interest report is a capital bridge folded from the partnership's own allocation runs, and it ties to them.

Reference partnership, 2025

| | REIT | Outside unitholder | Partnership |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Contributions | 400,000.00 | 100,000.00 | 500,000.00 |
| Income allocated | 33,340.20 | 8,335.05 | 41,675.25 |
| Closing capital | 433,340.20 | 108,335.05 | 541,675.25 |

The outside unitholder contributed a land parcel in kind for a 20% interest. The REIT's tests count 80% of the partnership's land and cash.

## Distributions and their tax character

Earnings and profits are computed separately from GAAP income. The computation starts from book net income and bridges to REIT taxable income line by line: book depreciation added back and tax depreciation taken, straight-line rent in excess of billed removed, unrealized gains removed, and recorded book-tax adjustments applied. Each line says where it came from, and the computation lists what it could not do. It is a computation and not a return. A taxable income figure your preparer supplies always overrides it.

Reference REIT, fiscal 2025

| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Book net income | 466,590.20 |
| REIT taxable income, computed | 476,692.12 |
| Earnings and profits | 483,852.70 |
| Distributions paid | 550,000.00 |
| Characterized as ordinary dividends | 483,852.70 |
| Characterized as return of capital | 66,147.30 |

Each distribution is characterized in the order the rules set: current earnings and profits first as ordinary dividends, then designated capital gain, with its unrecaptured Section 1250 part, then return of capital. The designations are the REIT's tax decisions and are entered, and the arithmetic keeps them honest. Each holder's categories sum to what that holder received, and each category summed over holders equals the category total, to the cent. With two holders at 60% and 40%, the first receives 330,000.00, of which 290,311.62 is ordinary and 39,688.38 is return of capital, and the second receives 220,000.00, of which 193,541.08 and 26,458.92. The 90% test on the same year passes at 550,000 against a 600,000 estimate.

A dividend reinvestment plan buys shares with the distribution at the class NAV strike, through the same capital engine as any other NAV-priced subscription. The distribution stays a distribution, with its character unchanged, and the reinvestment is a separate subscription linked to it.

## NAV REIT operations

A non-traded NAV REIT can run several share classes, each with its own servicing fee accrued on holder NAV in that class. The share repurchase program measures what each offer used against the monthly and quarterly caps, commonly 2% and 5%, reports the headroom and flags an offer in a window that is already over. It blocks nothing, because a board can suspend or waive a program. Each offer prorates oversubscribed requests and carries unfilled requests forward. The advisor's fee on NAV and its performance participation over a hurdle, with loss carryforward, run through the fee engine.

## FFO and AFFO, derived

FFO follows the NAREIT definition. It starts from net income, adds real estate depreciation and amortization, and removes gains and losses on the sale of depreciable real estate and impairments. AFFO then takes off the straight-line rent adjustment, tenant improvements, leasing commissions and recurring capital expenditure, read from the lease runs and the capex actuals. For an UPREIT, FFO is stated for the consolidated REIT and split between the REIT and the outside unitholders by income share. Adjustments for unconsolidated joint ventures are not modeled, and the pack says so on that line. Per-share figures are blank for a REIT kept on capital accounts rather than shares.

Reference REIT, first quarter 2025

| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Net income | 182,122.32 |
| Real estate depreciation | 54,000.00 |
| Real estate amortization | 2,958.90 |
| FFO | 239,081.22 |
| Straight-line rent adjustment | -3,780.82 |
| Tenant improvements | -109,500.00 |
| Leasing commissions | -36,000.00 |
| AFFO | 89,800.40 |

## Properties underneath

The REIT's properties use the same lease, rent roll and property-level accounting as any [real estate fund](https://1494labs.com/real-estate-fund-accounting/), including NOI, occupancy and weighted average lease term.

## What we don't do

We keep the books and track the tests. Tax returns, and the preparation and filing of Forms 1099-DIV with taxpayer identification numbers, stay with your preparer and transfer agent. The product computes the per-holder character and files nothing. Qualification decisions stay with your tax advisers. The 100-holder count rests on the investors the book holds, so a REIT whose beneficial owners sit behind nominees will need to supply them.

- [Registered fund accounting](https://1494labs.com/registered-fund-accounting/), which shares the repurchase-offer engine

- [Capabilities and status](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/)

Tell us how the REIT is structured, with or without an operating partnership, and how many share classes it runs. We will walk you through a quarter in the product.

# Secondaries and Strip Sale Accounting

For secondaries managers and administrators buying and selling LP interests.

## LP Interest Valuation and Reporting

- Valuations records dated marks for underlying fund interests, portfolio companies and priced instruments. The entry fields follow the asset: fund NAV statements carry an as-of date and source; company marks carry a valuation method and memo.

- Capital Accounts shows investor balances for the selected fund. Accounting checks compare investor capital snapshots with general ledger capital, giving the investor balances a defined tie to the fund's capital accounts.

- Investor statements show opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expenses, fees and ending capital. The statement draws these amounts from the investor's recorded account and the fund's reporting period.

- Underlying fund positions carry manager-reported marks and performance. Valuations and Look-through show position IRR, TVPI, DPI and RVPI, with support for late manager statements and the resulting restatement of reported values.

## Terms

Secondaries buyers use LP stakes or LP interests, reference date, purchase price, NAV discount and deferred consideration. GP-led and LP-led transactions include tenders, continuation vehicles and strip sales.

## Questions

### Can I record late manager marks and underlying-fund performance?

Yes. Underlying fund positions retain manager marks and position performance, including IRR, TVPI, DPI and RVPI. The valuation process supports late quarter statements and restatement of the affected reported values.

### Can I record dated marks for different investment types?

Yes. Valuations supports underlying fund NAV statements, portfolio company valuations and instrument prices. Fund statements record their as-of date and source. Company valuations record the valuation date, method and memo.

### Do investor capital accounts tie to general ledger capital?

Yes. The accounting checks compare investor capital balances with the fund's general ledger capital. Capital Accounts displays the investor balances. The tie is an accounting invariant checked across the book.

### Can an investor statement show flows, fees and ending capital?

Yes. The capital account statement includes opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expense, fees and ending capital. It records the period's movement for the investor account and its closing balance.

# Secondaries for Fund of Funds

For fund of funds managers and allocators handling continuation vehicles, tenders and LP-interest sales.

## Underlying Portfolio Reporting

- Valuations records dated marks for underlying fund interests, portfolio companies and priced instruments. The entry fields follow the asset: fund NAV statements carry an as-of date and source; company marks carry a valuation method and memo.

- Investor statements show opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expenses, fees and ending capital. The statement draws these amounts from the investor's recorded account and the fund's reporting period.

- Underlying fund positions carry manager-reported marks and performance. Valuations and Look-through show position IRR, TVPI, DPI and RVPI, with support for late manager statements and the resulting restatement of reported values.

- Look-through shows the underlying company holdings behind fund investments. It supports as-of views, shared ownership subtrees and CSV export. Company holdings supplied by import become part of the portfolio's underlying exposure view.

- Look-through groups underlying company exposure by geography and sector. The classifications come from linked company records, so the exposure view uses the recorded company classifications when presenting the portfolio totals.

## Terms

GP-led and LP-led secondaries include tender offers and continuation vehicles. Reference-date NAV, purchase price and interim cash flows describe the transaction; underlying manager marks and look-through describe the resulting portfolio.

## Questions

### Can I look through fund investments to the underlying companies?

Yes. Look-through presents company holdings behind underlying funds, including shared ownership subtrees and as-of views. Underlying holdings arrive by CSV import, and the look-through results can be exported as CSV.

### Can I group underlying company exposure by sector and geography?

Yes. Look-through reports sector and geography subtotals using the linked company records. Holdings without a linked company classification display a blank classification, allowing the team to identify those records.

### Can I record late manager marks and underlying-fund performance?

Yes. Underlying fund positions retain manager marks and position performance, including IRR, TVPI, DPI and RVPI. The valuation process supports late quarter statements and restatement of the affected reported values.

### Can I record dated marks for different investment types?

Yes. Valuations supports underlying fund NAV statements, portfolio company valuations and instrument prices. Fund statements record their as-of date and source. Company valuations record the valuation date, method and memo.

### Can an investor statement show flows, fees and ending capital?

Yes. The capital account statement includes opening capital, contributions, distributions, allocated income and expense, fees and ending capital. It records the period's movement for the investor account and its closing balance.

Source: https://1494labs.com/side-pocket-accounting/

# Side Pocket Accounting

For hedge fund managers and administrators accounting for side-pocket participation.

## Side Pockets and Dealing NAV

- Side pockets keep designated illiquid investments in total NAV and exclude each participating investor's pocket value from dealing NAV. The Side Pockets screen creates the pocket, previews and posts a carve-out, records investor participation and handles liquidation.

- The carve-out transfers the selected holding into the pocket and freezes the participating investors and their shares. Later subscriptions do not join that existing pocket. Pocket income and gains follow the recorded participants.

- Carve-out and liquidation previews show the proposed amounts before posting. A carve-out leaves total NAV unchanged. Liquidation records the disposal and distributions to the pocket's participants; the final liquidation closes the pocket.

## Supporting Accounting

- Share classes hold the terms for unitized funds. Fee classes group investors in capital-based funds. The Share Classes and Fee Terms screens record these arrangements for funds whose investors have different fee terms.

- NAV records preliminary, final and restated fund values, including share-class lines. The NAV and period-close screens show the fund's strike workflow, with class results available through the share register.

- Capital Accounts shows investor balances for the selected fund. Accounting checks compare investor capital snapshots with general ledger capital, giving the investor balances a defined tie to the fund's capital accounts.

- NAV supports share-class and series values, with final period strikes and daily estimates. Daily NAV estimates retain their grade and are superseded by the period close, preserving the distinction between daily and closed values.

## Terms

Side pockets are also called illiquid or designated investments and special situations. SP shares or classes describe participation. Dealing NAV is the value used for subscriptions and redemptions.

## Related Notes

- [Side pockets and investor participation](https://1494labs.com/notes/side-pockets-and-investor-participation/)

## Questions

### Does dealing NAV exclude the side pocket?

Yes. Total NAV includes the pocket's assets. Dealing NAV subtracts the investor's share of the pocket, using the participation recorded when the investment was carved out. The NAV records carry total NAV, side-pocket value and dealing NAV.

### Can I keep daily NAV estimates and final class NAV?

Yes. NAV supports daily estimates and final period strikes with share-class and series values. Daily estimates carry an estimate grade and are superseded by the close when final NAV is struck.

### Can investors in one fund have different fee terms?

Yes. Unitized funds use share classes, and capital-based funds use fee classes. The Share Classes and Fee Terms screens record these groups and their terms within the fund.

### Do investors who subscribe later join an existing pocket?

No. An existing pocket uses the participation recorded at its carve-out. Its income, gains and distributions follow those participants. A later subscription into the fund does not add that investor to the pocket.

### Can I preview a carve-out or liquidation before it posts?

Yes. Side Pockets provides previews for the selected carve-out and liquidation. Posting records the movement or disposal and the participant amounts. The carve-out preserves total NAV, and final liquidation pays the participants and closes the pocket.

Source: https://1494labs.com/waterfall-and-carried-interest-accounting/

# Waterfall and Carried Interest Accounting

For private equity managers and administrators calculating distributions and carry.

## Waterfalls, Carry and Clawback

- The distribution waterfall applies the fund's hurdle, catch-up and tiers, with European or American terms. Distribution preview shows the proposed GP and LP amounts. Posting records the distribution, and principal carry allocation uses the posted GP carry amount.

- Carry reporting distinguishes accrued carry from amounts already paid to the GP. Closed-end fund reporting calculates accrued carry from a hypothetical liquidation at the reporting-date NAV. Incentive fees also have accrual, crystallization and settlement records under the configured fund terms.

- Clawback measurement compares the GP's received carry with its entitlement under the fund's terms. The clawback test records excess carry, interest, escrow applied and prior repayments, and settlement records the GP's repayment for the investors.

- Carry Vesting records the GP's principals, their carry shares and vesting terms. Principal allocations use the vested fraction at the distribution date. Leaver events retain the effective date and treatment used in subsequent allocations and the vesting report.

## Supporting Accounting

- Waterfall setup records the hurdle, catch-up and distribution tiers for European or American carry arrangements. A policy preview shows the configured waterfall before it is used for the fund.

- Capital Accounts shows investor balances for the selected fund. Accounting checks compare investor capital snapshots with general ledger capital, giving the investor balances a defined tie to the fund's capital accounts.

- Allocations distributes income, expenses and gains through recorded ownership. The allocation screen includes a cascade preview and confirmation for structures with multiple ownership layers, connecting fund results with the investors above them.

- The company Exit screen calculates whole-holding exit proceeds through liquidation preferences, participation and caps. The calculation uses the company's capital structure to allocate the exit value across the security classes.

## Terms

Carried interest, preferred return, hurdle, catch-up and distribution tiers describe fund waterfall terms. European and American policies are available in waterfall setup. Company exit waterfalls use liquidation preferences, participation and caps.

## Related Notes

- [European and American waterfalls](https://1494labs.com/notes/european-vs-american-waterfall/)

## Questions

### Can I preview and post a distribution waterfall?

Yes. Distribution preview applies the fund's configured waterfall tiers to the proposed amount. The calculation shows the GP and LP allocations, including preferred return, catch-up and carry. Posting records the distribution in the books.

### Can I report accrued carry at the reporting date?

Yes. Closed-end fund reporting calculates the GP's hypothetical-liquidation entitlement at the reporting-date NAV and deducts GP carry already received, with a floor of zero. This accrued-carry amount appears in reporting; it is a report calculation.

### Can I measure a clawback and record repayment?

Yes. Clawback measurement and tests calculate the obligation under the configured fund terms, including escrow and prior repayments. Settlement records the GP's repayment. The final-liquidation workflow can run the fund's configured clawback test.

### Can a carry plan include vesting and leaver treatment?

Yes. Carry plans record principals, carry shares, vesting schedules and leaver treatment. Allocating a posted distribution uses the vested fraction for that date. The vesting report shows the principal-level results.

### Can I configure European and American waterfall terms?

Yes. Waterfall setup supports European and American policies, with hurdle, catch-up and tier terms. The policy preview calculates the configured distribution sequence so the finance team can review the terms.

### Can allocations follow several ownership layers?

Yes. Allocations supports period allocations and ownership cascades. The cascade dialog provides a preview and confirmation, and income, expenses and gains follow the recorded ownership chain to the participating investors.
